Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
10:00 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because paying becomes as easy as sending a text, and it costs users almost nothing. Since its launch in 2016, it has grown from a new idea into the usual way to pay, whether for a ₹10 cup of chai or a month's rent.

Three main reasons:

Speed and simplicity: Scan a QR code or enter a phone number, type your PIN, and the money moves in seconds, any time of day, even on holidays.
Free for most people: Paying friends and shops usually costs the user nothing. Small shops and street vendors can accept payments without a card machine.
One system, many apps: PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm or your bank's own app all work together, so you can pay anyone whichever app they use.

Trust helps too. Money goes straight from one bank account to another, so there is no cash to count and no wallet to top up. You also get an instant record of every payment. Cheaper smartphones and mobile data brought small towns and villages on board as well.

Cash hasn't vanished, but for many people it now feels slower and riskier to carry. Rules and fees can change, so check current details if you need exact figures.
